problem_summary.summary: Filter a target value out of an integer array in place; return the length of the kept prefix. The order of kept values may change.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: nums and val. Rearrange nums so its first k entries are not val, then return k; later entries are ignored.

brute_force.explanation: When a target is found, shift every later value one position left and recheck that index. This directly removes each match but can repeatedly move the same values.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Each shift closes one target's gap without changing the order of the remaining values; shrinking the active length excludes the now-irrelevant final slot.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) worst case — many removals can each shift a long suffix.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — shifts happen within nums.

optimized.explanation: Scan once and copy each non-target value into the next write slot. The write index is also the length of the kept prefix.
optimized.correctness_idea: After processing each input position, the prefix before write contains exactly the non-target values seen so far in their original order. Every input value is examined once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only index variables are added.

steps.action: Skip the target; do not advance write.
Copy 1 to index 0 and advance write to 1.
Copy 2 to index 1 and advance write to 2.
Copy 3 to index 2 and advance write to 3; return 3.

edge_cases.handling: The scan does not run and returns 0.
No value is copied, so the returned prefix length is 0.
Each value is copied to its existing position and nums.length is returned.
